text:
alex: Quick FYI, I just tried the onboarding curl example and it fails with 401.

alex: Example on page currently:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

alex: We should show the Authorization header or export an env var.

jess: I can take this. Do we want env var only or show both?

mike: Both. Show `export REDWOOD_KEY=...` then a curl using `-H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\"`. Safer than pasting tokens inline.

sam: Also add a one-line troubleshooting tip: if you get 401 check Authorization header / env var. Maybe include the minimal 401 JSON so it's clear.

jess: I'll open a tiny PR to add: (1) env var example, (2) header example, (3) single-line 401 note + sample response. Landing in ~20m.

docs-bot: Created issue #4523: \"onboarding guide: missing Authorization in curl snippet\" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/4523 :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks! Ping me on the PR and I'll validate in staging.

jess: Will do. I'll also @eng-oncall for a quick smoke after merge.

sam: If we want to prevent regressions we can add a tiny docs CI smoke test that runs the snippet against a sanitized staging mock. Filing follow-up for that.

jess: Good plan, follow-up issue welcome. Closing loop once PR is merged.
